chapter: Chicago bands and the Charlie Cook circle
title: Kentucky Midnight Serenaders and trumpeter Shorty Mack
summary: His five-piece band at 31st and State drew Armstrong and Oliver, featuring trumpeter Ray 'Shorty' Mack.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I wonder if you could tell a little bit about the first time you met Jolly Roll Martin. You say you remember him when you first came to Chicago.

First time, first time that I met him in person. I know him and seen him time and time again. I had a red hot five piece band at 31st and State and at that time I was called the Kentucky Midnight Serenaders and I was the first one that originated that day and the boys in the band was, they was all tops, that was all. Louis Armstrong and old man King Oliver didn't have nothing on my trumpet player and they used to come down there Louis, King Oliver and his whole band would come and watch us.
for this five, this trumpet player that I had then with me was Ray, Ray, Ray, Ray, Ray. It's Raymond and Ray. We called him Shorty Mack.
Shorty Mack. I'll find his name somebody else. We called him Shorty Mack. He was born
in Evanston and he had a kind of hunchola and it was short and he could play the sweetest trumpet with a mute in it in an apartment where we would go to some of them

and me always was knowing that we were very soft on piano and I'd play on soft piano and you could just hardly hear him play and he could play every jazz technique that Joe and Louis and he was Louis.
